verdict.rationale: Checkout.com documents paying with a token instead of raw card details. It also offers client-side public keys, a Hosted Payment Page and Flow components, which it markets as removing 'confusing compliance' and helping merchants 'stay compliant'. That implies a tokenized, low-PCI-scope integration path, but the pack never explicitly states that card data bypasses merchant servers or how far PCI scope is reduced. missing for 10: explicit documentation that card data never touches merchant servers, PCI DSS scope/SAQ-level guidance, client-side tokenization docs (e.g. Frames/tokens endpoint), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep my systems out of most of PCI DSS scope because card data is tokenized and never touches my servers

citations.quote: Request a payment using a token, a network token
No heavy lifting or confusing compliance.
helps you boost conversions, stay compliant
